content.text: 10 follow-up points were added (now 73 points over ~66 d). The 2-planet fit F4 (16.87 d + 11.34 d) failed submission on orbit match; refits are F16 (from F4), F17 (from F13: 11.8 d + 17.3 d), F18 (3-planet). Using the enlarged data: (1) what are the credible periods now, and are the two main signals really near 16.9 d and 11.3 d, or near 15.15/10.40 d or other aliases? (2) residual peaks of F16 with false-alarm probabilities, especially any long-period signal. Record an evidence note. Be fast (~2 min).

{"kind": "evidence", "text": "With 73 points, the data support two real signals, near 16 d and near 12 d, and nothing else. A two-planet fit (F16) leaves no significant residual peak, and no long-period signal. Thresholds below: a peak counts if its false-alarm probability is under 1%.
- Raw data: 16.04 d (false-alarm probability 5e-18) and 12.28 d (3e-5) are both real. No sampling aliases were found: the window function has no peaks. The 5.98 d peak (0.36) is roughly half of 12.28 d. It is a weak harmonic, not a planet, and may hint at some eccentricity.
- Peak position: the 65.5-day baseline only resolves periods to about ±2 d at 16 d and about ±1.2 d at 12 d. Two overlapping signals also pull each other's raw peaks. So 16.9 d and 15.15 d both fit the 16 d peak, and 11.3 d fits the 12 d peak. 10.40 d is about 1.9 d from the peak, which is marginal but not excluded. 17.3 d and 11.8 d (F13/F17) are also allowed. The periodogram cannot choose among these. Only the joint fit's likelihood or BIC can.
- F16 residuals (recomputed on all 73 points): the strongest peak is 2.56 d at a false-alarm probability of 0.048. That is above the 1% threshold, so it is not credible. All other peaks (2.81, 1.43, 1.38, 1.13, 2.24 d) are 0.31 or higher. Nothing is longer than the baseline. The only long peak in the raw data, 41.4 d at 0.79, is noise.
- What the new data change: the two signals are now much stronger. The residuals give no case for a third planet, so the 3-planet F18 is not supported unless its BIC clearly wins. A third planet would be suggested if the 2.56 d residual peak dropped below 1% after another campaign."}

content.text:
With all 73 points, two signals are real, near 16 days and near 12 days. The periodogram can't tell whether the exact periods are 16.9/11.3 or 15.15/10.40; only the fits can. A peak counts as credible here if its false-alarm probability is below 1%. I've recorded this as an evidence note.

**1. Credible periods (raw data)**

| Period | False-alarm probability | Confidence | Periods it could really be |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16.04 d | 5×10⁻¹⁸ | Very high | Anything from about 15 to 18 d, including 16.87, 15.15 and 17.3 d |
| 12.28 d | 3×10⁻⁵ | High | About 11 to 13.5 d, including 11.34 and 11.8 d. 10.40 d is a stretch |

- **No sampling aliases:** the observing cadence creates no false look-alike periods for either signal.
- **No new planet at 5.98 d:** that peak (false-alarm probability 0.36) is about half of 12.28 d, so it's a harmonic of the 12-day signal. It may hint that the 12-day orbit is slightly eccentric.
- **Why the exact period is open:** the data span only 65.5 days. That limits precision to about ±2 d near 16 d and about ±1.2 d near 12 d. Two overlapping signals also pull each other's peaks in the raw data.
- **What that means for the candidates:**
  - 16.9 d and 15.15 d are both inside the uncertainty of the 16-day peak.
  - 11.3 d is inside the uncertainty of the 12-day peak.
  - 10.40 d is about 1.9 d from the 12.28 d peak: unlikely but not ruled out.
- **What decides it:** compare how well each two-planet fit matches the data, using likelihood or the BIC score. That means comparing F16 (16.9/11.3 family) with F17 (17.3/11.8).

**2. F16 residual peaks (recomputed on all 73 points)**
- The strongest is 2.56 d, with a false-alarm probability of 0.048. That's above the 1% threshold, so it's not credible.
- The others are 2.81, 1.43, 1.38, 1.13 and 2.24 d, all at 0.31 or higher.
- There's no long-period signal, and nothing longer than the observing span. The only long peak anywhere is 41.4 d in the raw data, at 0.79, which is noise.

**Minimum planet count:** two. The 3-planet fit F18 has no support in the residuals, so only accept it if its BIC score is clearly better. Evidence for a third planet would be the 2.56 d residual peak dropping below 1% after another 10-point campaign.
